status: installed SDK transport boundaries verified locally; exact-source CI pending; no physical Storage acceptance
model_boundary: Actual installed StorageClient with injected synthetic fetch responses. globalThis.fetch throws; only the exact storage-contract.invalid endpoint/method is accepted. No key, Supabase connection, hosted account or real object store is used. Modeled apply-then-response-loss is a fault scenario, not evidence of actual server ordering.
findings: The installed SDK sends the exact upload path with x-upsert:false, but a 2xx upload body is not validated against expected Id/Key, actor, version or reviewed bytes.
An interrupted upload/delete response can report an error after the synthetic transport model has applied the write. The SDK issues no automatic retry in the tested default calls.
exists() for 400/404 returns false together with an error; 403/500 throws. No result distinguishes missing bytes from caller visibility, policy or stale metadata.

info() passes through server-provided metadata without binding it to the requested actor/path/object/version. download() returns bytes with no reviewed-hash attestation or If-Match precondition in the tested default request.

remove([exactPath]) sends DELETE with a prefixes array, but accepts empty, foreign or malformed successful response bodies. That request body alone does not prove server exact-match behavior or deletion.
The tested remove request carries no object-id/version precondition. Do not invent a conditional header or assume the storage server honors one.
limitations: No physical bytes, owner/version assignment, RLS, rollback, overwrite, exact-delete semantics, provider consistency or hosted acceptance is certified.
No new runtime adapter, receipt validator, endpoint, SQL proposal, state transition or cleanup capability is introduced. Twelve SQL proposals remain unapplied.
Current paths-only remove cannot be treated as verified exact-version deletion. Unknown results remain held; no automatic replay or prefix cleanup.
Related channel attachment removal paths remain a separate recorded review gate; this test does not fix them.
